precepts.text: The righteous is taken away from the evil to come; he enters into peace and rests in his bed, each one walking in his uprightness: Revelation 3:10.
precepts.point: Because thou hast kept the word of my patience I will keep thee from the hour of temptation which shall come upon all the world: Jacob's trouble leading into World War III and Armageddon. No force field; they are at rest. The righteous perisheth and no man layeth it to heart, but merciful men are taken away from the evil to come; they enter into peace and rest in their beds, each walking in his uprightness, and many that sleep in the dust shall awake. That is why when brothers and sisters die I do not do the tears.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Philadelphia means brotherly love, and that church was a colony of Israelites. Christ, “he that hath the key of David”, tells them: “behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it”. That open door is salvation. “For thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.” They were under persecution, so he says he will make the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet.

Then verse 10: “Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world”. The hour of temptation is Jacob’s trouble, which leads into the world war and Armageddon. The church of Philadelphia will not be there when it happens. Does that mean a force field around them? No. They are at rest.

Isaiah 57 shows it: “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” That is exactly what we just read in Revelation 3:10. “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.” Each one walking: they are not dead.

So when brothers and sisters die and people say, they keep dying, listen: I have a reason. They are at rest. You do your little tears and cry, that’s fine, but the Lord is keeping the righteous from the evil to come, the way he kept Philadelphia from the hour of temptation.

precepts.text: The high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity.
precepts.point: Time on earth began with the sun and moon on the fourth day, but with God a day is as a thousand years.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy”. The high and lofty One is the Father, and he dwells in eternity. Christ was with him in eternity in the beginning; the Word was with God. Christ did not create everything all at once on the first day. The Lord told him what to do, and he did it. Christ learned from his Father: what he saw his Father do, he was able to do.

“I dwell in the high and holy place”: that is above the heavens, above paradise, the holy of holies, the fourth floor, with restricted access. No man has been up there. He dwells there “with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.”

Sirach 18 explains eternity: “The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.” In eternity, where the Father is, a thousand years is like nothing. Those are the days of the Ancient of days. Sirach 1:2 says the same: “Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?” No one can count God's days. He exists outside of time, before time.

This goes with what Peter said: the days of Genesis are not earth days. They are measured from where the Father dwells, in eternity.

precepts.text: Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children.
precepts.point: Groves of trees are where the nations worshipped, and powerful men still gather at such places.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Isaiah shows what else was under the tree: “Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clifts of the rocks?” What were they doing under the tree? Slaying the children. Those children were gifts too. The children were the gifts under the tree, slain under the tree.

That is why they use the children to allure us in all the most popular holidays, Halloween and Christmas. They use the kids.

And the alluring works through gifts. Ecclesiasticus 20:29: “Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove”. We have Google and technology; we can easily look it up and see that it is pagan. But we are so covetous and want that self-gratification: Thanksgiving gift, Valentine's Day gift, New Year's gift, Halloween gift, Christmas gifts, the Easter suit. The gifts stop up the mouth, so a man who knows it is wrong and evil will not say anything, and will even fight for it. Many black and brown men will battle for hours for Christmas because they are married and scared to lose a vagina. The woman got you by the balls, and she's got your balls under the damn tree, gift wrapped. You offered a gift.

You cannot make it good; it's evil. The tree and the gifts under it go back to the idols Israel was commanded to destroy, and celebrating it is celebrating the destruction of your own people with your family.

precepts.text: The righteous perisheth and no man layeth it to heart, and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come, which is why Josiah is gathered in peace.
precepts.point: But because Josiah's heart was tender and he humbled himself, wept, and rent his clothes, the Most High will gather him to his fathers in peace so his eyes will not see the evil to come.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.”

That is why Josiah is gathered in peace. The Lord said through Huldah, “Behold, I will gather thee to thy fathers, and thou shalt be gathered to thy grave in peace, neither shall thine eyes see all the evil that I will bring upon this place, and upon the inhabitants of the same.”

The wrath was coming upon Jerusalem and “shall not be quenched”, and the righteous king was taken away from the evil to come.

precepts.text: The Most High addresses the seed of the adulterer and the whore who inflame themselves with idols under every green tree, who enlarged the bed, made a covenant with the heathen, and debased themselves even unto hell, stooping from the Most High down to idols made with hands.
precepts.point: As soon as she saw them with her eyes she doted upon them and sent messengers to them into Chaldea, going after them immediately.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Judah saw “the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion”, princes to look upon after the manner of Babylon, and “as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them”. She was enticed by the flashy artwork and gold, just as a harlot is enticed by a man flashing his wealth, and sent messengers to them into Chaldea immediately.

Isaiah speaks to that same seed: “draw near hither, ye sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the whore.” They are “children of transgression, a seed of falsehood, Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys”. Their portion is the smooth stones of the stream, to which they poured a drink offering. “Should I receive comfort in these?”

“Upon a lofty and high mountain hast thou set thy bed”. Behind the doors and the posts she set up her remembrance, “for thou hast discovered thyself to another than me, and art gone up; thou hast enlarged thy bed, and made thee a covenant with them; thou lovedst their bed where thou sawest it.” That is Judah: she enlarged the bed, made a covenant with the heathen, and debased herself even unto hell, stooping from the Most High down to idols made with hands. She loved their bed the moment she saw it.

points: The high and lofty one that inhabits eternity dwells in the holy place above, and also with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the heart of the contrite ones.

The Father and the Son deal and dwell with the humble in spirit; that to him is a sacrifice worth his time, and offering the best sacrifices while haughty is a complete waste of it. Humility comes before honour.
